title: Universal Scaling of the Spin Hall Effect
abstract: We study the spin Hall (SH) effect for the Dirac electrons in terms of the spin and magnetic-moment accumulation coefficients $-Γ^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy}$. We take short-range nonmagnetic impurities into account within the self-consistent $T$-matrix approximation. Similarly to the universal scaling for the anomalous Hall (AH) effect, we find three disctinct regimes by changing the electric conductivity $σ^{yy}$; the superclean regime with $-Γ^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy} \propto σ^{yy}$ owing to the skew scattering, moderately dirty regime with almost constant $-Γ^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy}$, and dirty regime with a new scaling relation $-Γ^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy} \propto (σ^{yy})^{0.6}$ whose exponent differs from that of the AH conductivity. Our results construct a unified theory of the SH effect without any ambiguity of spin current.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theory for the Spin Hall effect in Dirac electron systems by analyzing how spin and magnetic moment accumulation coefficients scale with electric conductivity. Using advanced Green's function techniques, the authors identify three distinct transport regimes—superclean, moderately dirty, and dirty—and establish a unified framework that differs from previous anomalous Hall effect scaling laws.
main_problem: The study investigates the scaling behavior of the Spin Hall (SH) effect for Dirac electrons, aiming to construct a unified theory that correctly defines spin current.
main_result: Three distinct transport regimes are found based on electric conductivity ($\sigma_{yy}$): superclean ($\propto \sigma_{yy}$), moderately dirty (constant), and dirty ($\propto (\sigma_{yy})^{0.6}$).
method: The analysis employs linear response theory using Keldysh Green's functions and the self-consistent T-matrix approximation to account for short-range nonmagnetic impurities.
model_or_system: The model is based on Dirac electrons, described by an anisotropic Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}(\mathbf{k})$), applied to systems like bismuth. Impurity scattering is treated via the T-matrix formalism.
key_observables: Spin Accumulation Coefficient (SAC) and Magnetic-Moment Accumulation Coefficient (MMAC); Spin Hall Conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}^{sz}$) and MMH conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}^{mz}$).
important_parameters: Electric conductivity ($\sigma_{yy}$), Fermi energy ($\epsilon_F$), impurity concentration, temperature ($T=0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the T-matrix approximation for impurities and involves deriving transport coefficients using vertex corrections (VCs) in the linear response formalism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Density of States (DOS), Fermi-energy dependence of SAC/MMAC, and crucially, the scaling relationship between SAC/MMAC and $\sigma_{yy}$ across the three distinct scattering regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops theoretical formulas for various transport coefficients using Green's functions in the T-matrix approximation. It then analyzes how these coefficients scale with conductivity ($\sigma_{yy}$) by identifying three distinct physical regimes, culminating in a unified theory framework.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the rigorous development of scaling laws and the need to define fundamental quantities (like spin current) in different scattering limits provides general theoretical tools applicable to open quantum systems dynamics.

figures.caption: Figure 3 shows the scaling relation between the electric conductivity and the SAC and MMAC. We choose ϵF > 0 to avoid the aforementioned sign change. Both these co- efficients have three regimes similarly to the AH conduc- tivity [12, 13]. In the superclean regime, the skew scatter- ing is dominant, and Γ00g xy sz and −Γ00g xy mz are propor- tional to σyy. In the moderately dirty regime, these coef- ficients are almost constant. Finally, in the dirty regime, we find a new scaling relation Γ00g xy sz , −Γ00g xy mz ∝ (σyy)0.6.
